info.title: Sylph Local Agent Runtime Service
info.description: Loopback-only, versioned API for durable sessions, turns, normalized events, and runner capabilities. Backend and agent-native session identifiers are never exposed in ordinary session responses.

get.description: Runtime state: session and turn counts, discovered and broken agents, every agent root considered, archive totals, live child processes, and the last retention pass. Authenticated, unlike /health, because it carries counts and local filesystem paths. The retention block's withheld/terminal pair separates correct behaviour from a broken pass — a terminal session is supposed to keep everything, while a delegated session that keeps withholding means the archive is not confirming it, and an all-unchanged pass means ingestion has stopped advancing. Its byte fields answer which session is growing, which the counts cannot: forty small withheld sessions and one enormous one report identically. bytesHeld is the logical record across every measured session rather than the footprint on disk, so it exceeds what du reports — a ranking measure, not a disk gauge. grewBy is signed, since negative means pruning worked, and is absent when a session has been measured only once, because one observation is not a trend and reporting zero would claim stability. There is deliberately no configurable size bound: a terminal session's record is the only copy, so a size-triggered prune is a size-triggered deletion of data nothing else holds.

Returns every resolved setting with the source that supplied it,. The same report `sylph-web-backend doctor` renders, served so the terminal and the settings panel cannot disagree. It exists because every failure in this area has one shape: a path resolves somewhere nothing lives, the server starts, /health reports fine, and the symptom appears layers away as a dead slash key. There is no adapter directory to report: adapters are compiled in, so which agents exist is answered per environment by GET /environments. A resolved value alone cannot distinguish a wrong path from a path that is not being read, so each entry names its source and the variable that overrides it. Read-only, deliberately: paths.browse_roots bounds where a spawned agent's current_dir may be, and therefore where arbitrary code may run, so a loopback HTTP surface able to rewrite it is a materially larger threat model than one that displays it — the config file stays the durable, reviewable record. Authenticated, since every value is an absolute local filesystem path.

200.description: The resolved configuration and its provenance

get.description: Returns the resolved SOUL.md with its path, size, and mtime. Exists because the toggle governing injection is meaningless without it: SOUL.md lives under the Sylph home directory, outside any other surface the app offers, so a user asked to consent to appending it has nowhere else to read it. A missing SOUL.md is a 200 carrying available:false rather than a 404 — an install without one is ordinary and runs every session natively, which the client has to be able to say. A file that resolved but cannot be read is a separate error field rather than a 5xx, because the settings panel must render the toggle either way. Resolved once in Config as paths.soul (~/.sylph/SOUL.md by default, overridden by SYLPH_SOUL, where an explicit empty value means no identity and a configured-but-absent path resolves to none).

200.description: Resolved identity text, or available:false when no SOUL.md exists

get.description: Sessions newest-activity-first. Filters are applied in SQL, not by the client: the listing is capped by limit, so client-side filtering would only narrow the truncated page. A blank filter value means unfiltered.

post.description: This starts an agent. It does not reserve a row. A session has no identity until an agent has assigned one, so there is nothing to create in advance: the CLI is spawned, the id it reports becomes the session's primary key, and the insert follows. That ordering is a behavioural change no schema can express, which is why it is stated here. What it deletes: DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id} for empties, the frontend probe that called it on unmount, and the window in which a session existed with no native id and therefore could not be resumed. A failed spawn now reports at the start screen instead of leaving a dead row behind. 502 AGENT_START_FAILED is the CLI not starting, or starting and reporting no id — the latter is a failure rather than a degraded success, because without an id the session could never be resumed and every link death would make it permanently unlinkable. 409 SESSION_ALREADY_PRESENT is the agent reporting an id that already names a session, which the primary key refuses: two rows for one conversation is the state it exists to prevent. `workdir` is bounded by configuration: it must resolve inside paths.browse_roots or the Quick Start directory, checked on the canonical path so `..` and symlinks are resolved rather than pattern-matched. The bound exists because this field is the current_dir of a spawned agent process and a coding agent reads and writes the tree it is pointed at, so it decides where arbitrary code runs — existence, the only property it was previously checked for, says nothing about whether it should. The same root set /api/v1/fs/* browses, deliberately: that endpoint exists to name a workdir, so a second bound would be a second thing to keep equal. With environments this check belongs in the envagent, because only the machine holding a path can canonicalize it. 403 POLICY_VIOLATION is a workdir that exists outside the permitted roots, distinct from 400 because the request is well-formed and the fix is in config.toml; the message lists what is permitted. The canonical path is journalled, so two spellings of one directory do not become two workspaces. A session already recorded outside the roots stays fully readable — nothing re-checks a journalled workdir, since narrowing configuration must not orphan history.

409.description: SESSION_ALREADY_PRESENT: the agent reported an id that already names a session.

502.description: AGENT_START_FAILED: the CLI could not be started, or started and reported no id.

503.description: ENVIRONMENT_UNREACHABLE: no envagent is connected for that environment.

post.summary: Adopt a session an agent already has
post.description: Brings in a session from the vendor's own native store on some environment. Replaces POST /api/v1/sessions/import, which named a row in a separate archive that no longer exists — so this is a different operation rather than a rename: the id is the vendor's, on a named machine, and nothing has to have parsed it first. watch: true follows the store as it grows, so a session running in a terminal right now appears and keeps updating and the 201 is answered before the transcript is complete; false parses one pass and is awaited, so a 201 means the transcript is readable. Policy-relevant fields are derived from the store, not the request. The working directory comes from the session's own recorded context and is bounded exactly like a created one — not belt-and-braces: a machine's store holds every session any agent ever ran there, so an unbounded adopt is a general way to start an agent anywhere. That the path came from the store rather than the request changes who chose it, not what happens next. The check produces the path that is journalled: a containment check paired with a path it did not produce is not a bound. fidelity reflects what the vendor's store actually holds — blocks or messages, never stream, read per session because a store can hold both. No care recovers a timing that was never written, so a renderer reads it before drawing a duration. injectIdentity defaults to false here, because the transcript so far was produced without it, but is settable: adopting a terminal session and injecting from that point on is a coherent thing to want. The derived title skips the agent's injected envelopes. The first user event is usually not what the user typed — agents prepend their own context as pseudo user turns — and taking it verbatim labels most sessions with boilerplate byte-identical across every session of that agent; skipping those raised recognizable labels from ~10% to 98% over 311 measured sessions. Measured limit on that fallback: no adapter carries the user's typed text for claude or codex, so their opening ask is not in the stream at all — claude is titled by its own recorded title (~93% of sessions) and codex adopts untitled. Errors are six and deliberately distinct, because the fixes are: 400 nothing to do, 403 widen configuration, 404 wrong id, 409 already done, 422 unusable source, 503 bring the machine online. Collapsing any pair sends a reader to the wrong layer.

201.description: The session, with fidelity reflecting the store.

400.description: No such agent on that environment, or the recorded workdir no longer exists.

403.description: POLICY_VIOLATION: the recorded workdir is outside that environment’s roots. The message lists what is permitted.

404.description: NATIVE_SESSION_NOT_FOUND: that environment's store has no such session. Distinct from SESSION_NOT_FOUND, which is about Sylph's own store — the code is what says which store to look in.

409.description: SESSION_ALREADY_PRESENT: adopting twice would produce two rows for one conversation. Checked before the agent is, so a session already held on a since-uninstalled agent reports “already done” rather than “install that CLI”.

422.description: NATIVE_SESSION_NOT_RESUMABLE: the store recorded no working directory, so there is nowhere to run it. Guessing one is not available as a fallback, because a workdir is the current_dir of a spawned agent.

503.description: ENVIRONMENT_UNREACHABLE: no envagent is connected for that environment.

get.summary: What native sessions an environment holds
get.description: Answers “what is on this machine” without adopting anything, which is what makes adopt offerable in a UI rather than requiring a user to know a vendor id. Answered from the envagent's local stores. A session already adopted is marked as such rather than hidden or offered: hiding it leaves a user hunting for a session plainly on the machine, and offering it hands out a 409 nobody can act on. The same applies to a session whose recorded workdir is outside the permitted roots or absent — blocked carries which, so a picker shows the row and says why instead of failing on click. Rows are newest-first on whichever stamp the store carried; a session with neither sorts last, because an absent stamp is a store that has not settled rather than a session from 1970. Paging: cursor is opaque and must be echoed back unparsed, never constructed. It indexes into a snapshot held for 30 seconds, which is what makes a walk self-consistent — these files are being written while a user pages, so an offset into the live store would silently skip rows that moved to the front and serve others twice. Measured cost of one listing pass on a real machine: pi 531 rows in 90 ms, claude 1000 in 1.81 s, codex 1258 in 3.51 s, so ~5.6 s for the machine and 29 ms per page thereafter. Two of the three read more than a header per file on purpose — claude a 32 KB head for its own title, codex a 256 KB tail for the last stamp — which is why the figure is not the 164 ms a header-only pass costs.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: Required: there is no privileged machine, not even the one the server runs on.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: One agent, or every readable one when omitted. Naming an agent with no native store is a 400 rather than an empty list, because an empty list is indistinguishable from “that agent has no sessions here” and the two have different fixes.

parameters.name: workdir
parameters.description: An exact path match after normalizing trailing slashes, never a substring: the store this replaced compiled it to LIKE '%…%', so /w/app also matched /w/app-old and every subdirectory.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Echo back nextCursor unparsed. A cursor this endpoint did not issue is refused rather than treated as zero, because silently restarting a paged scan is how a client loops forever over page one.

200.description: What that environment holds, newest first.

400.description: Malformed environment id, an agent with no native store, or a foreign cursor.

503.description: ENVIRONMENT_UNREACHABLE: no envagent is connected for that environment.

patch.summary: Update a session's per-turn flags or title
patch.description: Flags are validated against the agent's own `--describe` schema on write, rather than being dropped silently at turn time. A flag the agent does not declare, or a value outside an enumerated flag's `choices`, is rejected. An empty `choices` list means the flag is free-form and only its name is checked. If the session's runner is no longer installed its flags cannot be validated, so they cannot be changed — failing is better than storing a value that would be discarded later. Both fields are optional; sending neither is a no-op.

200.description: The session after the update. Previously `$ref`'d CreateSession — the *request* schema — so a generated client typed this response as the body it had just sent.

get.description: FTS5 over the archive. Answers "which archived session mentioned X". Never 503 when the archive is unreachable — it is optional locally, and an empty result with availability reported elsewhere keeps a sidebar working. This is the one archive read that must never go per-row: search is ~200 ms while every other operation is microseconds to sub-millisecond. It covers only what a parser read, so it does not cover Sylph-born history whose native store the server never saw.

200.description: Hits, or empty when the archive is unreachable

get.description: Reconnectable SSE stream. Last-Event-ID is accepted as an alternative to after_seq. Stable journal replay precedes live projection events.

200.description: SSE stream. Each frame is named after its event kind (event: thinking), so a client must not dispatch on EventSource.onmessage, which receives only frames named message.

Cache-Control.description: Always 'no-cache, no-store, no-transform'. no-transform (RFC 9111 5.2.2.6) forbids an intermediary from re-encoding the body; without it a compressing proxy gzips the stream and buffers the whole turn into one delivery.

get.summary: Sessions rolled up by working directory
get.description: Backs the left sidebar and the settings panel. Derivable from GET /sessions except for two facts only the server has: the absolute Quick Start directory (requires expanding ~) and counts spanning more sessions than the LIMIT-capped session listing returns. The Quick Start directory is always present, even with no sessions.

200.description: Workspace roll-up, newest first by lastUsedMs

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description: Also report directories that exist only in the TraceDB archive, with archivedCount set. Off by default: the sidebar polls this endpoint and needs only live sessions, while the scan walks every archived session. Surfaces where the user picks a directory pass it, because a project they are about to work in has no live session yet. An unreachable archive degrades to live-only rather than failing.

get.summary: List one directory level in a session's working directory
get.description: Read-only. `path` is relative to the session workdir; omitted means the root. One level per request, because walking a 100k-file repository server-side spends seconds building a payload whose first screen is all that is read. Containment is enforced on the canonicalized path, so `..` and symlinks cannot escape the workdir; escaping symlinks are omitted from listings entirely. Machine-generated directories (.git, node_modules, target, .next, and similar) are never listed.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory relative to the session workdir. Empty or omitted lists the root.

200.description: Directory listing, directories first then case-insensitive by name

post.summary: Upload one file into the session's working directory
post.description: The upload root is the session's journalled `workdir`, not the configured browse roots: the agent driving the session already writes anywhere under `workdir`, so this grants no new capability, while allowing uploads anywhere the directory picker can reach would give the browser a wider write range than the process it drives. `name` is sanitized to a single path component, so a filename cannot carry a directory. Refuses an existing file unless `overwrite` is true.

delete.summary: Delete one file or directory from the session's working directory
delete.description: The only irreversible operation in this API: there is no trash to restore from, because reaching the platform's trash means a new dependency or spawning a host process. Three guards hold for any client, not only this project's UI. The workdir root is refused with 403, since path='', '.', and '/' all normalize to it and a client bug sending one would erase the project. A non-empty directory is refused with 400 unless recursive is true; an empty one needs no flag. A symlink is unlinked rather than followed, which requires canonicalizing the parent and appending the final component verbatim - canonicalizing the whole path would resolve the link and delete its target instead.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Entry to delete, relative to the session workdir. The root itself is refused.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Required to delete a directory that is not empty.

post.summary: Create one directory in the session's working directory
post.description: Its own route rather than a mode of POST .../files: one takes a body of bytes and the other a name, and a handler switching on which field is present is how an upload with a typo'd key silently becomes a mkdir. Non-recursive, and it refuses an existing path rather than succeeding quietly, so 'New folder' twice reports the collision. The name is rejected rather than rewritten when unusable - a separator, '.', '..', a control character - deliberately unlike the upload sanitizer, which strips non-ASCII: that is right for an incidental filename and wrong for a folder the user is naming, where a CJK name silently becoming 'attachment' is invisible data loss.

get.summary: Read one file from a session's working directory
get.description: `encoding` is decided by whether the bytes decode as UTF-8, not by the file extension, so a .log holding binary output is reported as binary rather than rendered as mojibake. Text over 1 MiB is truncated to a 256 KiB prefix. An image over 1 MiB is not served at all, since a partial image decodes to nothing; it returns encoding=binary with truncated=true.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: File relative to the session workdir.

200.description: File contents, or metadata alone for binary and oversized files

get.summary: Read a spreadsheet, CSV, Word document, or PowerPoint deck as structure
get.description: Parsed server-side, because the npm alternative (SheetJS 0.18.5) is unmaintained with two unpatched High CVEs on this exact parse-untrusted-input path and is 7.5 MB unpacked against a ~4 KB first-load budget. The response is a union on `kind`: `grid` for .xlsx/.xlsm/.xlsb/.xls/.ods/.csv/.tsv, `blocks` for .docx/.pptx. Spreadsheets are windowed — `rows` defaults to 200 and caps at 500, and an out-of-range window is clamped rather than refused, since a 50000x30 sheet takes ~600ms to materialize and would be a ~50 MB response. Files over 25 MiB are refused before parsing; a zip part is bounded both by its declared header size and by the actual read, because the declared figure is attacker-supplied.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: File relative to the session workdir.

parameters.name: sheet
parameters.description: Worksheet index for grid formats. Out of range is INVALID_REQUEST.

parameters.name: row
parameters.description: First row of the window, 0-based and absolute within the sheet.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Rows to return. Clamped, not refused, and the response echoes what was served.

get.summary: Read a file's bytes, for content the browser renders natively
get.description: Serves the file's bytes whole - nothing on this route is truncated, which is what makes it the target of 'open in a new tab' for a file the pane can only preview in part. Content-Type has three tiers: an allowlisted type is served as itself; anything else whose bytes are text is served as text/plain (never its own text/* label, so smuggled markup is shown as source rather than executed); everything else is application/octet-stream with Content-Disposition: attachment. Tier 2 asks the bytes, not the extension, so .svelte and .rb render while a .log full of binary downloads. The response headers are load-bearing: serving workspace HTML from this origin without Content-Security-Policy: sandbox lets a script in an agent-generated file read the sylph_session cookie. SVG is never served as image/svg+xml, because at that type a script inside it runs in our origin; it is text, so a tab shows its source, and the pane renders it through the /files/content base64 path inside an instead. Content-Disposition always carries the filename, taken from the canonical server-side path and sent in both RFC 6266 spellings, because a download without one saves as 'raw'.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: File relative to the session workdir.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: Force Content-Disposition: attachment. Separate from the type allowlist because the allowlist decides what is safe to render and this decides what the user asked for; without it Download on a PNG opens a tab showing the image.

200.description: The file's bytes, with inert-type and sandbox headers

Content-Security-Policy.description: Always `sandbox`, so the response occupies an opaque origin however it is loaded.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: Always `nosniff`, so an octet-stream payload cannot be sniffed into text/html.

ETag.description: Derived from mtime and size, paired with Cache-Control: no-cache so a re-view revalidates and an agent's edit is noticed.

get.summary: List the directories that may be browsed
get.description: `$HOME` plus `SYLPH_BROWSE_ROOTS`. This is the only endpoint that tells a client what it is allowed to enumerate, which is why widening the variable widens what any client of this backend can see. `home` is reported separately because a browser cannot expand `~` for itself.

get.summary: List subdirectories of one browsable directory
get.description: Directories only, one level per request. There is deliberately no `/fs/content`: this surface exists so a user can name a workspace, and enumerating directory names is a strictly smaller disclosure than serving bytes — reading bytes stays session-scoped, where the root is journalled rather than chosen. A symlink leaving the permitted roots is omitted from the listing rather than merely refused, so it is never advertised as a node to try. `parent` is absent when the listed directory is itself a root, which is what stops a client offering a 'go up' that would leave the permitted set.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute path to list. Defaults to the first configured root.

200.description: Subdirectories, with the canonicalized path listed

get.summary: Every paired environment, and what it can run
get.description: Replaces GET /api/v1/agents. Which agents exist is per environment, not global: a user picking an environment with no codex on it should learn that before creating the session rather than after, and a merged list would be true of nowhere. Availability is PATH, not a handshake. An agent is available when its CLI is on that machine's PATH. There is no discovery pass, no adapter directory, and therefore no broken map — that mechanism produced two total silent failures in this repo's history, the worse being that zero discovered agents made / a dead keystroke three layers from the cause. “Why can I not use this agent” now has one answer with one fix. reachableVia is not decoration: a non-null value means this environment is reachable only while the named one relays for it, so control dies when that machine leaves. Rendering it identically to a directly-connected environment would promise AFK continuity it cannot keep. An empty agents array is a real answer — an envagent with no vendor CLI on its PATH — and a client must render it as “nothing installed here” rather than as a loading state.

200.description: Every paired environment, whether it is connected, and its agents.

get.description: Sets the `SameSite=Strict` HttpOnly auth cookie for a loopback client, which is why the frontend must proxy `/api/v1/*` same-origin: a browser will not send the cookie across ports. Exempt from auth, alongside `/health`. The token is regenerated on every backend start, so open browser sessions are invalidated by a restart — that is the design, not a bug to fix by persisting the token.

get.summary: What this session's agent can do
get.description: Establishes a link as a side effect. A failed handshake is 200 with `attached:false` and a typed `failure`, not 5xx: it is the agent's failure, not the request's, and the session's history stays readable. Do not cache indefinitely — see api-design.md § Links.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

post.description: Its own operation because establishment is slow (an agent CLI loads a project), so a UI can pay the cost before the user finishes typing. Unlike /capabilities a failure here is an error, because establishing was the whole request.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

delete.summary: Tear the link down without ending the session

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

post.summary: Ask the agent to stop producing
post.description: Session-scoped, not turn-scoped: it acts on the agent, and the session is what holds a link. A turn-scoped route would force a caller to know a turn id to interrupt the only turn running.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

post.summary: Send guidance into a running turn

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

post.summary: Queue text to run after the turn in flight
post.description:
A follow-up, not a correction. `steer` reaches the agent *inside* the running turn; this is read after it ends, and queueing with nothing running is a coherent ask that becomes the next turn's opening text. So there is no `turnId` precondition: a turn boundary crossing underneath this changes nothing.

Requires `Capability::Queue`. An agent without it answers 409 `UNSUPPORTED_FIELD`, which a client renders by retiring the control rather than leaving it clickable.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

200.description: The text was accepted for after the running turn

post.summary: Set a typed session config value
post.description: A refusal distinguishes UNSUPPORTED_FIELD (no such option; disabling the control is justified) from INVALID_VALUE (this value, right now; leave it usable). A client must render the refusal — a mutation with only a success path makes a rejected set look like a dead control.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

200.description: Surface after the set, with currentValue from the vendor confirmation

get.description: SSE. Lives on the server because reconstruction is subtle enough that doing it per frontend would let two frontends disagree about what one history means.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

get.description: A link attaching or dying, capabilities changing, a request raised or retired. Distinct from the turn stream, which exists only while a turn does. A pending request is published on every transition including its departure, and the payload is the row (carrying `status`) rather than the transition.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

get.summary: What this session is waiting on, oldest first
get.description: Read from the journal rather than from the link, so it answers after a reconnect, from a different frontend, and for a session whose link has since died — which is exactly when a user needs to know why nothing is happening.

schema.description: The identity triple `<environment>:<agent>:<native_id>`, percent-encoded as one path segment. Not a UUID: a native id is the vendor's own value and may contain `/`. See § A session id in a path is the identity triple.

post.summary: Answer a request an agent raised
post.description: The answer is validated against the request's declared form. Answering against a dead link still retires the request everywhere, because the claim is what makes the answer final.

FilterOrigin.name: origin
FilterOrigin.description: Closed set; an unknown value is rejected with 400 rather than yielding an empty list.

FilterWorkdir.name: workdir
FilterWorkdir.description: Case-insensitive substring of the working directory.

Query.name: q
Query.description: Free-text query; whitespace-only is treated as absent.

nativeId.description: The vendor's own id for the session, unchanged.

watch.description: Follow the store as it grows rather than parsing one pass.

title.description: Overrides the title derived from the opening ask.

injectIdentity.description: Defaults to false: the transcript so far was produced without it.

ArchiveCounts.description: Archive-wide totals, or null when the archive is unreachable. Here rather than in /health because it is a count and /health is unauthenticated.

BlockedReason.description: Why this row cannot be adopted, absent when it can. Typed rather than prose so a client branches on it: alreadyAdopted navigates to the session Sylph already holds, outsideRoots names a configuration fix, and noWorkdir cannot be made adoptable at all. Each is one of the adopt errors decided before the request rather than after, so a picker cannot disagree with the endpoint.

BlocksPayload.description: Word and PowerPoint share this shape: a slide is a section whose blocks follow it, so one renderer serves both. A structured list rather than Markdown or HTML — Markdown would mean escaping prose containing * or _ or | on the way out and re-parsing it on the way in, and HTML would reintroduce an innerHTML path into a frontend built to avoid one.

sections.description: Slides for pptx; empty for docx, which has no equivalent division.

title.description: From the shape whose placeholder type is title or ctrTitle.

index.description: 0-based position in presentation order, which comes from p:sldIdLst resolved through the presentation rels — not from sorting filenames, since slide10.xml sorts before slide2.xml.

notes.description: Speaker notes from the per-slide ppt/notesSlides part.

firstBlock.description: Index into `blocks` where this section's content begins.

key.description: Dotted key as it appears in config.toml.

source.description: Which source won. Precedence is environment, then file, then a default derived from the root.

envVar.description: The variable that overrides this setting, named here so acting on the row needs no table elsewhere.

exists.description: Whether the path is there. ABSENT rather than false for settings that are not paths — a log level rendered as missing reports a working setting as broken. A bare command name (the tracedb.bin default) is checked against PATH, since a filesystem check would call a working install absent.

home.description: The one root every path defaults under.

configPath.description: The file to edit. Shown so a user knows what to open.

configPresent.description: False before a first run seeds it, and after a user deletes it. Stated rather than implied, because a table of values needs to say when none of them came from a file.

environment.description: Which environment runs the session, as the opaque id minted at pairing — never a hostname, because a name in a key means renaming destroys identity. Required rather than defaulted: which agents exist is per environment, decided by what is on that machine's PATH, so there is no global default that would be true anywhere. Restricted to base32 (a-z, 2-7), which is what lets the encoded session id be split on its first two delimiters unambiguously.

injectIdentity.description: Whether SOUL.md is appended to the agent's prompt. Accepted here and refused by PATCH: a transcript records what produced it, so rewriting the flag would rewrite what the stored history means. This replaces identityMode and lifecycleMode, which were a pair of four-valued enumerations with exactly one behavioural read between them — the SOUL path choice. A boolean also keeps the property the closed enumeration existed for: a non-boolean is a 422 naming the field, rather than a value nothing downstream matches that would read as "not sylph" and silently disable injection.

DiagnosticsResponse.description: Authenticated: exposes counts, agent names, and local filesystem paths.

activeTurns.description: Turns the supervisor is running right now. Was `activeProcesses`, which named a process count and always held a turn count — harmless only while every process was one Sylph spawned.

level.description: Heading level 1-6, or list nesting depth for listItem.

text.description: Plain text, for headings and list items.

spans.description: Runs of text with inline formatting, for paragraphs.

ordered.description: For listItem: numbered rather than bulleted.

rows.description: For table: rows of cell text, first row being the header.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page. Absent when this page is the last.

streamId.description: Stable id for one logical block across its phases. A tool_result repeats its tool_call's id so the two group.

span.description: The delegated trajectory this event happened in; absent is the root turn. A subagent event's streamId is itself a trajectory id, so a nested delegation names another here. See docs/session-protocol.md, Delegated trajectories.

name.description: Tool name for a tool_call, or the agent's own name for a subagent trajectory.

isError.description: Set on a failed tool result, a failed trajectory, or an error event.

Event.description: A normalized stream or journal event. Kinds are additive by protocol, so a client must tolerate one it does not know rather than rejecting the stream.

size.description: Full size on disk, even when the body is truncated.

encoding.description: Derived from the bytes, not the extension.

mimeType.description: Extension-based guess. Advisory: selects a viewer, never access.

content.description: Text, or base64 for images. Absent for binary and oversized images.

FileDocumentResponse.description: A parsed document. `kind` discriminates the payload: exactly one of `grid` or `blocks` is present, matching it.

format.description: The concrete container, so the header can say "Excel workbook" while the viewer switch stays a two-way branch.

path.description: Relative to the session workdir. The root itself is the empty string.

size.description: Files only; omitted for directories, where it means nothing.

isSymlink.description: A listed symlink always resolves inside the workdir; escaping ones are omitted.

path.description: Parent directory relative to the workdir. Empty means the root.

name.description: New directory's name, one path component. Rejected rather than rewritten when unusable.

path.description: Relative to the workdir, as the Artifacts pane addresses entries.

root.description: Absolute canonical path of the session workdir.

path.description: The directory listed, relative to the workdir.

truncated.description: True past 2000 entries in one directory.

path.description: Destination directory relative to the workdir. Empty means the root.

name.description: Filename; sanitized to one path component.

data.description: File bytes, base64, no `data:` prefix — the same encoding turn attachments use.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file. Absent or false refuses instead.

path.description: Relative to the workdir, as the Artifacts pane addresses files.

parent.description: Absent when `path` is itself a configured root.

path.description: Absolute, because the client hands it back as a `workdir` or as the next directory to list.

v.description: The string to display. Dates are already ISO-8601, never an Excel serial. Per-cell currency and percent formats are not reproduced: calamine folds the number format into the value and exposes no format string, so only date-vs-number survives.

t.description: Drives alignment — numbers and dates right, text left.

n.description: Raw value for a number cell, so the client need not re-parse a formatted string.

f.description: The formula expression, when t is formula.

sheets.description: Every sheet with its true dimensions, so the client can report what it is not showing. A single entry for CSV and TSV.

exact.description: False when the sheet declared no <dimension> element and the totals were counted rather than read.

sheet.description: Index of the sheet actually served.

row.description: First row of the window served, absolute within the sheet.

rows.description: The window. Each entry is one row of cells; a null cell is empty, which is most of a sparse sheet.

hasHeaderRow.description: Advisory: whether the first row of the sheet looks like headers.

truncated.description: True when the sheet holds rows beyond the window served.

HealthResponse.description: Unauthenticated, so it reports availability only — never counts, names, or paths. `agents.available` is here because a server with zero agents answers every other probe successfully while no session can run and no command can be offered, so liveness alone reports healthy for a process that cannot do its job.

schemaVersion.description: Highest applied migration, read from `_sqlx_migrations`. It is not a hand-maintained number: an `app_meta` copy used to be bumped by migrations and four of them forgot, so the field answered its one question wrongly.

available.description: Unreachable is a supported configuration, not a failure: live sessions work and archive features report themselves unavailable. Deleted when the archive becomes an embedded crate, since nothing external will answer.
Whether any agent is usable at all. A boolean rather than a count, to keep this endpoint free of anything an unauthenticated caller should not learn.

code.description: Closed vocabulary so a UI can choose its own words and offer the right recovery. `no_adapter` is the one a retry cannot fix. Both values describe *Sylph's own spawn* failing, so neither can yet express an adopted session — a process running fine that is not ours to drive.

message.description: Always populated, so an unrecognized code still renders.

LinkState.description: Live link state. An empty `supports` means Sylph cannot reach the agent, never that the agent has no capabilities — for an adopted session the process is alive and simply not ours.

supports.description: Empty when detached: capability is a property of a live link, and a remembered list would promise interrupt on a session Sylph holds no channel to.

capabilities.description: Commands, config, permission mode, context window. Facet-scoped by protocol: an unmentioned facet is never cleared.

failure.description: Present only when establishing was tried and failed. Not cached — the next read tries again.

NativeSessionRow.description: One native session an environment holds. Every field an adapter cannot answer is absent rather than defaulted: a synthesized title or timestamp is a lie a journal makes permanent, and this row is what a picker renders.

workdir.description: Where it ran. Absent means the store recorded none, which makes the session not resumable — adopt answers 422 rather than guessing a directory to run an agent in.

title.description: The vendor's own recorded title, when it keeps one. Measured: claude ~93% of sessions, codex and pi none.

endedAtMs.description: Last recorded activity. Absent while a session is still being written — an absent end is not an ended session.

eventCount.description: How many events one pass would yield, when the store can say cheaply.

parentNativeId.description: The session this one was delegated from or forked out of, as the vendor recorded it. Not derived from an id-naming convention: the /agent- suffix recovers 8.8% and misattributes on a collision.

fidelity.description: What parsing this session would actually yield. Per session rather than per agent, because a store can hold both. Never stream.

id.description: The encoded triple this row would adopt as. Always present, including on a blocked row — it is what a client navigates to for an already-adopted session.

PendingRequest.description: Something the agent is waiting on. A resource rather than a stream message, because the agent blocks until answered — so it must outlive every client and be answerable from a frontend that attached an hour later. Note what is deliberately absent: the adapter's own request id. It is scoped to one link and means nothing to a client, and exposing it would invite a client to send it, which is a way to answer a request that was never raised.

id.description: How a client addresses this request.

detailJson.description: The proposed input, as a JSON string.

optionsJson.description: Offered options, as a JSON string.

formJson.description: The input this request declared it wants collected. Absent means an approval, whose subject is one proposed tool input rendered from `detailJson`. A client must not sniff `detailJson` for field names it recognizes — only the agent knows what it is asking for, which is why a form is declared rather than inferred.

allowPersistent.description: When false the client must omit "always allow" entirely: the agent has said a lasting grant would be broader than this ask. Persisted rather than held on the link, because the dialog may be rendered by a client that attached long after the request was raised.

expiresAtMs.description: Advisory. Nothing server-side acts on it.

status.description: Reconcile against this rather than against a vocabulary of verbs — a status added later then needs no client change.

queued.description: Always true; a refusal arrives as an error envelope rather than false.

text.description: The follow-up to run after the current turn. Must not be blank.

input.description: An edited version of what the agent proposed. This is what makes "allow, but change the command" work — a real terminal affordance a yes/no dialog drops. Absent means as proposed.

RetentionPassReport.description: The last retention pass. Reported because retention's correct behaviour is usually 'nothing was dropped', which is indistinguishable from a broken pass without the counts: `withheld` beside `terminal` separates a session that is supposed to keep everything from one the archive is not confirming, and an all-`unchanged` pass means ingestion has stopped advancing.

SearchHit.description: One lineage-collapsed archived session. TraceDB scoring internals (score, scoreBreakdown, bm25) are deliberately not exposed: they carry no UI meaning and would couple this API to TraceDB's ranking implementation.

sessionId.description: Live session id when this archived session was already imported, so the UI can offer open instead of a duplicate import.

available.description: False when TraceDB could not be reached at all.

detail.description: Why the archive is unavailable. Absent when available.

Session.description: A session as every session-returning endpoint serializes it. Mirrors `backend/src/models/session.rs`. Note `nativeSessionId`: the field is `backend_session_id` in Rust and renamed on the wire, so a reader looking for the Rust name in this document will not find it.

id.description: Sylph's own id, and the only id any route uses. Disjoint from the archive's `<agent>:<native-id>` space; comparing the two is silently always-false.

origin.description: `sylph` means Sylph spawned the adapter and holds its stdio; `native` means somebody else started the process. Immutable after creation, and the axis every capability question resolves on.

identityMode.description: Whether `SOUL.md` is injected. Fixed at creation and refused by PATCH, because it describes what stored history was produced by.

lifecycleMode.description: Written to the journal and read by nothing today. See architecture.md § Session Origins before relying on it.

nativeSessionId.description: The agent's own session id, used to resume. Absent until the agent reports one.

traceSessionId.description: Archive id this session was imported from, `<agent>:<native-id>`. Present only for an imported session, and serialized so the archive browser can tell an archived row is the same conversation as a live one.

workdir.description: Canonical working directory of the spawned agent, derived from the containment check rather than from the request string.

flagsJson.description: Agent flags as a JSON string, not an object. Serialized as stored.

SessionEnvelope.description: Every single-session response wraps the session under one key rather than returning it bare.

SessionListResponse.description: Capped server-side. Do not assert on a count against a shared home; assert on identity.

value.description: Opaque by contract — a token the agent enumerated and the client echoes back, never something to parse. This is what lets a composite encoding change with no client change.

SoulResponse.description: The identity text Sylph appends to an agent's prompt. Read from disk per request rather than cached at startup: SOUL.md is hand-edited between sessions, and a cached copy shown beside a toggle claiming to control the live file would be stale.

available.description: A readable SOUL.md resolved. false means every session on this install runs on the agent's own identity whatever the client requests, which the UI needs to state plainly rather than offering a toggle over nothing.

path.description: Absolute path, so the user can go edit it.

content.description: The text as the agent receives it, absent when the file resolved but could not be read.

bytes.description: Size on disk, before any truncation.

truncated.description: Present only when true: content holds just the first 128 KiB, cut on a char boundary so the tail is not rendered as U+FFFD.

error.description: Why no content is present, when a path resolved but could not be read. Distinguishes "there is no SOUL.md" from "there is one and it is unreadable" — different problems with different fixes.

turnId.description: The turn the client believes is running. Optional: a client with no turn in view is steering whatever is running, which is a coherent ask.

Turn.description: A turn as the API serializes it. Mirrors `backend/src/models/turn.rs`. `origin` is the field that stops a client rendering an answer to a message the user never wrote: an `agent` turn is one nobody asked for, opened when an agent speaks after its previous turn settled, and its `requestText` is empty by construction.

status.description: A turn's lifecycle state. The four terminal values -- completed, failed, cancelled, interrupted -- mean the turn's record is finished, not merely that the agent stopped: a client that reads one of them can fetch the turn's history and find everything. settling is in flight, and is the state a turn holds while the server closes what it left open.

origin.description: Who started it. Not a synonym for the session's `origin`.

errorCode.description: One of the 25 codes in ErrorResponse's enum, at exact parity with the Rust vocabulary.

TurnWithEvents.description: Events oldest first. `delta` events are never included: they are transient by protocol and their text is already in the matching `completed` event, so replaying both would duplicate every token.

flags.description: Per-turn agent flags, e.g. `model`, `effort`. Validated against the agent descriptor.

path.description: Absolute path. Display shortens it; API calls need the real value.

lastUsedMs.description: Newest updatedAtMs across the workspace's sessions. 0 when it has none.

isQuickStart.description: True for the configured Quick Start directory, which the sidebar lists separately.

archivedCount.description: Archived sessions TraceDB holds for this directory. Always 0 unless the request passed includeArchived, so 0 means "not counted" rather than "no history".

quickStartDir.description: Absolute path of the Quick Start directory, resolved server-side: the browser can neither expand ~ nor know what paths.quick_start_dir was set to.

dataDir.description: Where the journal and attachments live.

home.description: Used client-side to abbreviate paths as ~/...
